feed.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories
feed.subtitle: Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.

entry.title: South Korea to recall its ambassador to Ukraine over North Korean POW dispute
entry.summary: The South Korean announcement on Thursday came days after its President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified punitive steps if Ukraine refuses to apologize over the revelation.

entry.title: South Korea test-flies its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon
entry.summary: The test follows North Korea's recent hypersonic missile test. Tensions between the Koreas have increased after land mine explosions injured three South Korean soldiers near the border. North Korea denies responsibility.

entry.title: Strike on Ukrainian public bus leaves 30 dead as blackouts worsen in Kyiv
entry.summary: Russian strikes in eastern Ukraine have killed 30 people and injured at least 18, according to authorities. The attacks included a strike on a public bus and have worsened power outages in Kyiv.

entry.title: ICE has quietly used this warehouse as a detention facility all summer, neighbors say
entry.summary: Throughout the summer, rumors have been bubbling in North New Jersey that ICE has quietly been using a warehouse as a detention center. NPR investigated.

entry.title: Medical debt is crushing hospital patients in LA. Health officials may have a fix
entry.summary: In Los Angeles County, the nation's most populous, a new system could screen hospital patients for financial aid, preventing hundreds of thousands from getting bills they can't pay.

entry.title: Flock is catching flak. Experts say other police surveillance tools are more worrisome
entry.summary: Real-time crime-center software is a sometimes overlooked but powerful tool allowing police to aggregate immense amounts of data, significantly expanding their surveillance reach.

entry.title: As crypto and prediction markets expand, their regulator shrinks
entry.summary: Even as the agency is tasked with drawing up new rules for crypto and prediction markets, its staffing and enforcement actions have dropped precipitously during the second Trump administration.

entry.title: Syrian general accused of atrocities is protected by U.S. and Lebanon, NPR and BBC find
entry.summary: A former Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity is living quietly in Lebanon, bankrolled and protected by American and Lebanese authorities, a BBC/NPR investigation has found.

entry.title: Toss-ups, triage and targets: How to read the wide-open 2026 House map
entry.summary: Both parties are spending heavily in roughly 60 House districts — where Trump won by an average of 9 points in 2024 — that could be key to deciding control of the chamber, an NPR analysis finds.

entry.title: How 'Musk' director Alex Gibney became a critic
entry.summary: A trove of documents and interviews with people close to tech billionaire Elon Musk reveal a damning picture of his rise as one of the world's richest and most powerful men.
